findings.title: Add a consumer-composable SelectPanel parts surface
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer needs to own the trigger, panel layout, input, list, and footer actions beyond the current item/data configuration.
findings.observedGap: SelectPanel exposes an item-configured component and function-only renderAnchor; docs report no subcomponents for a consumer-composable panel.
findings.additiveFix: Add an opt-in parts entry point while retaining the existing config/data API, renderAnchor signature, and defaults. Keep exact part names/default elements pending review.

findings.title: Align the shared open-state contract
findings.reachableUseCase: Consumers use SelectPanel and ActionMenu together and need a predictable shared open-state name and default model.
findings.observedGap: SelectPanel requires open while ActionMenu documents open as optional with default false.
findings.additiveFix: Align the new parts APIs on one open/defaultOpen model and shared default chosen by maintainers; preserve both legacy root contracts and their callbacks.

findings.title: Order configured SelectPanel classes component-first
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer supplies className for the action list rendered within SelectPanel.
findings.observedGap: The configured FilteredActionList combines consumer className before its component class, contrary to ADR-025.
findings.additiveFix: Keep the current configured class behavior during migration; use the required ordering for the new parts and preserve existing public props.

findings.title: Place SelectPanel styles in the component cascade layer
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer applies utility-layer styles to SelectPanel; unlayered component rules do not participate in the declared Primer layer order.
findings.observedGap: The authored CSS Module contains no cascade-layer declaration, although ADR-021 and ADR-022 require component styles to use the named primer.components layer.
findings.additiveFix: Place the component style rules in @layer primer.components.SelectPanel; retain any globally scoped registrations and all existing selectors and declarations.

findings.title: Document each composable part
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer assembles SelectPanel.Root with parts and needs to learn each part’s owner, props, ref behavior, and supported composition path without reverse-engineering examples.
findings.observedGap: The composition stories demonstrate layouts, but SelectPanel.docs.json still declares an empty subcomponents list and there is no per-part reference for required props/state/refs.
findings.additiveFix: Add part-level API documentation and component metadata while keeping the configured SelectPanel docs and entry point unchanged.

findings.title: Add as support to every part
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer needs a custom semantic element for a trigger, content region, list, or leaf part while retaining the part behavior.
findings.observedGap: Only Title exposes as; Root, Trigger, Overlay, Content, Header, Description, SearchInput, List, Item, Group, and the action/form parts do not expose a uniform as contract.
findings.additiveFix: Add an additive as prop to each rendered part and preserve its required props, state, accessibility attributes, and final ref; resolve the DOM-less Root contract with maintainers rather than exempting it silently.

findings.title: Separate handler skipping from preventDefault
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer handles Trigger, Item, or action-button events and needs to prevent Primer behavior without cancelling the browser default, or skip later handlers without changing DOM cancellation.
findings.observedGap: Part handlers run consumer-first, then use event.defaultPrevented to decide whether Primer state behavior continues; the separate consumer skip contract is absent, and no render-element handler stage exists.
findings.additiveFix: Add one shared part merge path with the specified render-element → part-consumer → Primer order and a distinct skip method; preserve DOM preventDefault and state cancel as separate signals.

findings.title: Align configured and part class merging with their surface policies
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer supplies className to the configured action list or to a composable SelectPanel part and expects the documented precedence for that surface.
findings.observedGap: The configured action list combines consumer className before its component class, while new parts put Primer classes before consumer classes. Both paths miss their respective accepted merge order.
findings.additiveFix: Keep the existing configured behavior available while adding an opt-in or versioned migration to ADR-025 order; use consumer-first classes on new parts. Preserve current props and callback signatures.

findings.title: Expose and merge refs consistently across parts
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer needs the rendered DOM node from Root, Overlay, or Group for focus, measurement, or integration.
findings.observedGap: Root and Group are ordinary function components, and Overlay accepts an overlayProps ref rather than a part-level forwarded ref; several rendered parts therefore lack a uniform consumer ref contract.
findings.additiveFix: Forward and merge every consumer/internal ref to its final rendered element; decide and document the Root ref behavior alongside its required render contract.

findings.title: Add the object-shaped state transition callback contract
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer controls or observes open and selected state and needs the originating event, reason, and synchronous cancellation before an uncontrolled commit.
findings.observedGap: The new Root callbacks are positional; onOpenChange receives (open, reason), onSelectedChange receives only the array, and requestOpenChange commits before invoking onOpenChange.
findings.additiveFix: Add the target object callback with value, reason, optional event, and synchronous cancel while preserving the existing configured SelectPanel callback signature and keeping callback naming explicit.

findings.title: Resolve failing composable interaction behaviors
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer opens an unanchored modal, removes the focused option, dismisses a nested supplemental dialog, or uses the opt-in configured adapter inside Dialog.
findings.observedGap: The focused SelectPanel directory run has 7 failures among 1688 tests; rerunning the matching cases with one worker reproduces all 7 across adapter fallback, focus repair, nested dismissal, and modal visibility.
findings.additiveFix: Keep existing configured callbacks and props; correct the failing overlay, focus, and adapter behaviors, then rerun the focused suite until all cases pass.

findings.title: Add stable selectors to each public part
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer or component test needs to identify Trigger, Content, List, Item, or other named parts without depending on generated CSS classes.
findings.observedGap: The new public parts do not emit their own data-component identifiers; the only SelectPanel-prefixed selector in SelectPanelParts.tsx identifies a nested secondary-action affordance.
findings.additiveFix: Add stable data-component identifiers to the root element of each part and cover them in the part tests and API docs.

findings.title: Place SelectPanel component styles in the named cascade layer
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer combines component styles with utility-layer rules and expects Primer’s declared layer order to determine precedence.
findings.observedGap: The component, overlay, platform, and virtualized collection CSS Modules contain no @layer declaration.
findings.additiveFix: Wrap runtime component styles in @layer primer.components.SelectPanel while retaining existing selectors and declarations.

findings.title: Add Storybook Playwright coverage for the composable API
findings.reachableUseCase: A consumer interacts with SelectPanel.Root and the new parts in a Storybook story and expects the keyboard, focus, and overlay behavior to remain stable.
findings.observedGap: The existing SelectPanel Playwright suite visits configured stories only; the new composition stories have Vitest coverage but no Playwright interaction scenario.
findings.additiveFix: Add a focused Playwright test that visits a composable SelectPanel story and exercises the trigger, filtering, selection, dismissal, and focus-return path.

findings.title: Align the shared open-state contract
findings.reachableUseCase: Consumers use SelectPanel and ActionMenu together and need a predictable shared open-state name and default model.
findings.observedGap: SelectPanel requires open while ActionMenu documents open as optional with default false.
findings.additiveFix: Align the new parts APIs on one open/defaultOpen model and shared default chosen by maintainers; preserve both legacy root contracts and their callbacks.
